newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem challenges Cavallo to prove charges in court.
newsitem.headline: Menem challenges Cavallo to prove charges in court.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem Tuesday challenged former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo to prove his accusations against two cabinet ministers in court.

"All courts in the country are open," Menem told local news agencies after Cavallo, whom Menem fired almost three months ago, accused the interior and justice ministers of trying to to cover up graft probes and manipulate judges.
"We have no interest at all in picking an argument with Cavallo ... who of course will have to prove what he says," Menem said.

Cavallo told a local radio station from New York, where he is teaching economics at a university, that both Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan were manipulating the courts.

Corach once wrote on a paper napkin the name of several judges and state prosecutors and bragged, "These do as I say", said Cavallo, who was sacked last July after one of many clashes with Menem over his austerity policies.
"Jassan used to call judges and prosecutors to give them instructions on issues he was interested in," added Cavallo, the architect of Argentina's economic reform plan.

Because of ministers like Corach and Jassan, "The feeling is that there is neither security nor justice in Argentina," said Cavallo, who last week announced he will run for Congress in 1997, but not for Menem's ruling Peronist Party.

In a seven-point statement, Corach rejected the charges, calling them "totally irresponsible and reflecting (Cavallo's) state of emotional imbalance." He also said he had issued instructions for immediate judicial action.
A spokesman for Jassan said the justice minister had no immediate plans to react to Cavallo's charges.
